CA-08.001: people make visual objects, sounds, movements and stories that can express experiences and carry knowledge. a song can accompany work or a celebration. cloth can protect a body and reflect skills or meanings learned among its makers. games can be recreational and also teach shared rules or skills. knowledge about making things and organizing daily life can pass between people through language, imitation, demonstration and participation. habits vary between households and communities. a museum record of a musical instrument and a photograph of weaving document different practices. each leaves out sound, movement and the wider circumstances of use. cultural meanings may differ among participants and change over time. some practices and records carry restrictions set by communities, and an archive needs their context and permissions. material culture tradition
CA-08.002: communities can pass knowledge and expression through storytelling, song and performance. words, melody, rhythm, movement and the relationships among participants can all matter. a story may take different forms when told at different times or by different people. a recording can preserve one event. it can lose the ways people learn a performance, collaborate in it or decide when it is appropriate. in the unesco convention on living heritage, communities and practitioners have roles in identifying and safeguarding their practices. a record about one tradition needs its own context. the archive contains a photograph of one dance performance and a record of one musical instrument. these visual objects convey limited information about rhythm, sound and community meaning. oral tradition performance
